Democrats’ victory sparked concerns that tighter regulation could slow the AI infrastructure buildout that has helped lift stocks to record highs this year.Nasdaq fell 6%, marking its worst drop since the infamous Covid-19 crash in March 2020. The tech-heavy index also entered a technical ‘correction’ territory, a 10% drop from ⁠its October 6 record-high close.Nvidia shares plunged more than 9%, while the Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index crashed over 12%. The selloff wiped off $3 trillion in stock market value from S&P 500 companies. articles.title: Nithya Raman elected Mayor of Los Angeles
articles.summary: New York: Indian-born democratic socialist Nithya Raman has been elected Mayor of Los Angeles, scripting history as she becomes the first South Asian mayor of the nation's second-largest city.Raman, 45, who was a Los Angeles City Council member, defeated incumbent 73-year-old Karen Bass in the November 3 mid-term elections.Also read: Democrats' US midterm sweep may give India more room to negotiate a balanced trade deal with TrumpWith this victory, America's two largest cities - New York and Los Angeles - are now run by Indian-descent mayors who are Democratic Socialists."Los Angeles, I am deeply honoured to be your next Mayor. Thank you to the thousands of people who knocked on doors, sent texts, made phone calls, convinced their neighbours to believe in the promise of this big, beautiful, joyful city that we get to call home," Raman said in a video posted on X Thursday.Raman paid tribute to her predecessor Bass, the first woman mayor of Los Angeles, for her decades-long public service."I am going to City Hall to work every single day to earn your trust and to earn your trust in this city again. And that work starts now, so that we can build housing that people can afford, parks for our children to play in, a transit system that can get people where they need to go, a city that is safe for its working people and its families, and a city government that is actually capable of delivering on its promises," Raman said.LA City Councilmember for District 4, Kerala-born Raman is an urban planner by training, and she received her bachelor's degree from Harvard and a graduate degree from MIT.Raman is among the several Indian-American candidates who have emerged victorious across the country in the US midterm elections that concluded Tuesday and delivered a significant rebuke to President Donald Trump and the Republicans as the Democrats gained control of the House and Senate, flipping seats and traditional party strongholds in a massive blue wave across America.Also read: Marco Rubio weighs leaving administration after GOP’s midterm lossIndian American Impact, an organisation that empowers South Asian and Indian-American communities through community engagement, civic partnerships, and candidate support, congratulated Raman on her victory in the general election for Mayor of Los Angeles.Noting that Raman will become the first South Asian American mayor of the nation's second-largest city, the Indian American Impact said her victory reflects the growing political power of South Asian Americans in California, a state with more than one million South Asian residents, the largest such population in the country.Executive Director of Indian American Impact Chintan Patel said in a statement that Raman ran on lowering rents, building housing faster, and making city services work for Angelenos, and voters chose her to deliver it."With her win, South Asian Americans will lead the two largest cities in the United States," Patel said, referring to New York and its Mayor Mamdani.The 5.5 million-strong Indian-American community registered significant political gains in the midterms, with several candidates from the community winning historic elections to various positions across the country.Pia Dandiya of Florida and Dr Amish Shah of Arizona will be the newest Indian-American members of the US Congress, with their victories speaking to the "growing political power of our communities."They will join Representative Ami Bera, Representative Pramila Jayapal, Representative Ro Khanna and Representative Suhas Subramanyam at Capitol Hill."At a time of rising hate against our communities, representation matters, and they will fight to keep our communities safe," Indian American Impact said. "All six are committed to lowering costs for working families, expanding access to health care, and protecting immigrants, and they will serve as a powerful check on the Trump administration in the next Congress," the organisation said.Among the other notable election victories are that of Manoj Chourasia, who has been reelected to the New Hampshire State House, Darshana Patel who won her reelection to the California State Assembly, Ranjeev Puri whose won reelection to the Michigan House of Representatives.With Democrats retaking the chamber, Puri is expected to become Michigan's next Speaker of the House, which would make him the first Indian American Speaker of a state House in the country.Dr Krish Subrahmanian won his election for the Minnesota State Senate; Aruna Miller has been reelected as Lieutenant Governor of Maryland; Lisa Kaul won her election for the New York State Senate, defeating a Republican incumbent and flipping a seat in New York; and Nabeela Syed won her election for Illinois State Senate District 26.Amar Mukunda won his election to the Maryland State Senate; Saba Haider has been elected to the Illinois State House; Josh Kaul has been re-elected as Wisconsin's Attorney General; Pooja Sethi won her election to the Texas House, District 47, becoming the first Indian American to serve in the Texas legislature; and Jyot Singh has been elected to the Georgia State House, District 97, the first Indian American and first Sikh American elected to the Georgia State Legislature.

M-cap of BSE-listed companies tops Rs 500 lakh crore mark
articles.summary: Mumbai: The combined market capitalisation of all companies listed on the BSE crossed ₹500 lakh crore for the first time Thursday, reaching around ₹502 lakh crore ($5.31 trillion) amid a broad-based rally in equities and a steady addition of newly listed companies.It took 622 trading sessions for the total mcap to rise from ₹400 lakh crore, first crossed on April 8, 2024, to the latest milestone. The mcap first crossed ₹100 lakh crore on March 12, 2014, and took 1,494 sessions to reach ₹200 lakh crore on February 4, 2021. The ₹300 lakh crore milestone was reached on July 6, 2023, after another 586 sessions, while the subsequent rise to ₹400 lakh crore took 181 sessions.135589318The latest milestone is significant because it comes even as the benchmark Sensex and several broader market indices remain below their record highs. The Sensex is still 7.6% below its peak of 85,836, recorded on September 26, 2024.The BSE MidCap 150 is 5.3% below its record of 17,373, reached on August 26, 2026, while the BSE SmallCap 250 is 8.4% below its peak of 7,514, recorded on September 23, 2024. The BSE MicroCap 250 is 7% below its record of 19,988, reached on September 8, 2026.Read more: Why Nithin Kamath believes NRI investing in India has become easier than everA steady stream of initial public offerings (IPOs) has also contributed to the expansion of the overall mcap, even as several benchmark indices remain below their peaks. In 2024, 94 companies made their mainboard debut, adding around ₹12 lakh crore to mcap on their listing days. In 2025, 115 companies listed, adding nearly ₹14 lakh crore, while 107 companies have listed so far in 2026, adding above ₹25 lakh crore."The large number of IPOs has added to the overall mcap. At the same time, several companies outside the main indices have participated in the rally, helping total mcap reach a record even as major indices remain below their peaks," said Ankur Punj, MD, Equirus Wealth.The latest milestone has also coincided with a sharp recovery in equities. The Sensex and Nifty have gained more than 8.1% each in six consecutive sessions. The BSE MidCap 150 has advanced over 8.4% in eight of the past nine sessions, while the BSE SmallCap 250 has risen around 7% in seven of past eight sessions.Read more: Titan Q2 Results: Profit jumps 54% YoY to Rs 1,722 crore; total income up 25%The rally has been supported by a decline of more than 19% in crude oil prices over the past three sessions, easing concerns over inflation, India's import bill and the rupee. Strong foreign portfolio investor (FPI) buying, with net inflows of over $3.4 billion in the past 12 sessions, positive global cues, reduced uncertainty following the US midterm elections and better-than-expected second-quarter earnings have also lifted investor sentiment."The momentum could continue in the near term if crude prices remain stable at lower levels and foreign inflows sustain. However, investors should remain cautious as geopolitical developments, crude price volatility and profit booking after the sharp rally could limit further upside," said Ravi Singh, chief research officer at Master Capital Services.

articles.title: Demat account additions hit 9-month high in October as IPO boom draws investors
articles.summary: Mumbai: New demat account additions rose to a nine-month high in October, marking the fourth monthly increase in five months after a prolonged period of moderation between January 2025 and May 2026, as robust IPO activity drew more investors to the stock market.NSDL and CDSL together added nearly 3.36 million demat accounts in October, the highest monthly addition since January 2026. The total number of demat accounts stood at around 244 million at the end of the month. The number of demat accounts does not represent unique investors, as individuals can hold multiple accounts. The number of unique investors is estimated at around 136.6 million as of September, according to NSE data.Robust primary market activity was a key driver of the increase, with several large and smaller public issues attracting retail participation. October was the busiest month for IPO activity in 2026, with 13 issues raising a record ₹44,507 crore, including the Jio Platforms IPO - India's biggest ever.Read more: Why Nithin Kamath believes NRI investing in India has become easier than ever"Demat account openings typically rise when there is a surge in IPO activity, as investors open accounts to participate in public issues. The recent listing activity, including the large Jio Platform IPO and several smaller issues, has contributed to the increase," said Sunny Agrawal, head of fundamental equity research at SBICAPS Securities.Growing interest in gold and silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs) has also encouraged retail investors to open demat accounts, Agrawal said. Investors can purchase these products through the secondary market using a demat account.Read more: Equity mutual fund inflows may drop 18% in October as midcap and hybrid funds lose momentum: NomuraThe pickup in demat account additions came with gains in benchmark indices, with the Sensex rising 2% and the Nifty gaining 1.9% in October. articles.title: Fed's Beth Hammack and Thomas Barkin favour gradual rate hikes as inflation stays high
articles.summary: Federal Reserve officials Beth Hammack and Thomas Barkin are making the case for a gradual approach to interest rate increases, signalling that policymakers remain focused on bringing inflation under control even as uncertainty over the economic outlook grows, Reuters reported.Their comments on Thursday come as the US central bank faces competing pressures from persistent price increases, geopolitical tensions and heavy investment in artificial intelligence (AI). The remarks also mark the first round of comments from Fed officials after Democrats won control of Congress and made gains in state level elections. For live updates on US Markets, click here "I expect that monetary policy will need to move to a restrictive stance to bring inflation back to 2% in a timely manner," Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland President Beth Hammack said in a speech ahead of an event in Zurich.According to Reuters, Hammack, a consistent supporter of higher borrowing costs, favours smaller and more frequent adjustments rather than sharp increases. She said this approach would be less disruptive to households, businesses and financial markets. Gradual increases could also prevent an “inflationary mindset” from taking hold, she added.Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin echoed that view, saying inflation remained “too high” and was holding firm rather than easing. "When it comes to the pace of future rate hikes, gradual makes sense," he said.Inflation keeps pressure on the FedThe comments follow the Fed's decision last week to keep its benchmark interest rate in the 3.75%-4.00% range. Hammack, along with Fed Governor Lisa Cook, voted in favour of a rate increase, highlighting the divide among policymakers over how aggressively to tackle inflation.Also Read: Emerging markets lose $33.8 billion in October as investors flee Asian stocksFinancial markets broadly expect another increase in December, although expectations beyond that remain less certain. Reuters reported that futures traders have lowered the probability of a December hike to around 70% from more than 80% on Wednesday.AI investment and elections add to uncertaintyThe political shift could also influence the inflation outlook. Local voter opposition to data centres and permitting challenges could slow AI infrastructure spending, potentially easing demand for equipment and related resources.Evercore ISI analysts told clients on Wednesday that AI capital expenditure could slow in the next year or two, helping keep demand and supply in balance without requiring many more rate increases.TD Securities said it expects the Fed to raise rates by another 50 basis points by early next year. However, the brokerage said a resolution to the Iran war or a slowdown in AI investment could reduce the need for further tightening after March.Meanwhile, Friday's US jobs report is expected to provide another test for policymakers, with economists forecasting 65,000 additional jobs in October after September's 29,000 gain, Reuters reported.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

articles.title: LTCG cut may come with a separate tax tweak
articles.summary: New Delhi/Mumbai: Key stakeholders are offering divergent prescriptions on how to address concerns over long-term capital gains tax (LTCG) tax and securities transaction tax (STT).These include scrapping LTCG altogether, removing it just for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs), or lowering the rate. As for STT, suggestions include reducing it for some products and increasing it for others, people familiar with the discussions said."A well thought-out call would be taken," said an official. Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman has said she will consider investors' concerns regarding LTCG. These measures are being considered as a way of stemming the exodus of overseas investors that has led to a slump in Indian stock markets.While the LTCG collections amounted to ₹1.29 lakh crore in FY25, those for STT stood at ₹57,522 crore. Any call on the levies would have to take into account the revenue impact and funding for social sector schemes and subsidies.Finance ministry officials have met senior market participants to seek their views on capital market taxation. ET had reported on October 28 that the finance ministry officials had reached out to stakeholders on the issue.Financial sector regulators including the Reserve Bank of India and the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) are understood to have backed the idea of doing away with LTCG to make India an attractive destination for foreign investors.Most participants favoured abolishing LTCG on equities while suggesting that the government could consider a marginal increase in STT on options trading alone, leaving cash and futures transactions untouched. They argued that options account for the bulk of daily trading activity and have been the focus of regulatory efforts to curb excessive speculation, people said.Some participants have cautioned against extending preferential tax treatment to FPIs alone, saying such a move could draw criticism from domestic investors. Short-term capital gains on listed equities, held for up to one year, are currently taxed at 20%, while long-term gains on holdings exceeding one year attract a 12.5% levy.Foreign portfolio investors have argued that several competing markets in the region do not levy LTCG, putting India at a disadvantage.Market participants said the combination of rupee depreciation and capital gains taxation has weighed on foreign investors' dollar-denominated post-tax returns, making other markets more attractive. One of the suggestions that has been put forth is calculating an FPI's taxable capital gains in dollar terms rather than rupees, said one of the persons.Separately, some FPI representatives also sought simplification of procedures governing the inflow and repatriation of foreign capital, calling for easier processes to bring funds into India and take money out of the country. Market participants said senior finance ministry officials have patiently heard out their suggestions.Another official said the implications of all suggestions would be examined before a final decision is reached.

articles.title: Mehli Mistry challenges Tata Trust exit
articles.summary: Mumbai: Former Tata trustee Mehli Mistry has challenged his removal as a trustee of Bai Hirabai Jamsetji Bai Hirabai Charitable Institution (BHJTNCI), arguing that the decision was invalid and that some trustees who voted against his reappointment were themselves ineligible.In a series of rejoinders filed with the deputy charity commissioner for Greater Mumbai Region, Mistry has argued that the trust deed does not prescribe a fixed tenure for trustees or specify citizenship or tax residency as a qualification for trusteeship.He also accused Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) of attempting to prevent scrutiny of alleged governance lapses, including commissions and financial benefits received by trustees. The matter has been adjourned to December 3. Challenging the recording of his cessation as a BHJTNCI trustee with effect from October 28, 2025, Mistry argued that neither the trust's 1913 will nor its 1923 trust deed prescribes a fixed tenure for trustees.The trust's position that his three-year term had expired relied on a 2022 circular and appointment letter, but neither of them can override the governing instruments, he argued.Citing Clause 23 of the deed, Mistry said vacancies arise on grounds including death, permanent residence outside the Bombay Presidency, insolvency, renunciation of faith and unfitness, but not on expiry of a fixed term. The codicil also says trustees "shall always be trustees," he added.Mistry argued that he is not a "tenure trustee" under Section 2(17A) introduced through an 2025 amendment and that Section 30A(1), therefore, does not apply to him. He also cited the trust's annexures, which allegedly show different renewal periods for other trustees, including about two years for Vijay Singh and less than two years for Venu Srinivasan."The trust cannot use Section 30A(1) as a sword to oust the objector on October 28, 2025, and, in the same breath, ignore that very provision when its own vice chairman (Singh) acted in breach of it on that very day. A party cannot approbate and reprobate," Mistry said in his submission.He also cited a resolution passed on October 17, 2024, at a joint meeting of SDTT and Sir Ratan Tata Trust trustees, shortly after Ratan Tata's death. The resolution provided for trustees to be reappointed on expiry of their terms without any limit on tenure, he said.The trust deliberately omitted it from its reply to his complaint, Mistry claimed.He urged the authority to reject BHJTNCI's change report against him as "illegal, non-est and contrary to the trust deed."According to Mistry, Circular Resolution No 671 of October 23, 2025, proposing his reappointment, was approved by Jehangir H C Jehangir and Darius Khambata but was not approved by Noel Tata, Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh. articles.title: US jobless claims hit 57-year low
articles.summary: WASHINGTON: The number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment slipped to a 57-year last week as layoffs remained low against the backdrop of a resilient labor market.Initial claims for state unemployment benefits fell 6,000 to a seasonally adjusted 189,000 for the week ended October 31, the Labor Department said on Thursday. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast 196,000 claims for the latest week.Claims matched the 189,000 level touched in mid-July, which was the lowest reading since 1969.They have stayed mostly below 200,000 since mid-September.Low layoffs, thanks to strong domestic demand and profit growth, are anchoring the labor market, with hiring still constrained by uncertainty over the dragging US-Israeli war with Iran.The government reported this week that there were 1.06 open jobs for every unemployed person in September, up from 1.02 in August, which some economists argued was a sign of the labor market starting to tighten. Others, however, viewed the low level of jobless claims as a function of a smaller labor force amid an immigration crackdown, rather than fewer job cuts.A separate report from global outplacement firm Challenger, Gray and Christmas on Thursday showed US-based employers announced 43,994 job cuts in October, up 2% from September. Planned layoffs dropped 71% compared to October 2025.Despite the rise over the month, layoffs were the lowest for any October since 2023. Employers announced plans to hire 444,692 workers last month, a 57% jump from October 2025. Hiring plans were the highest for any October since 2009, and likely mostly seasonal jobs."Employers are holding on to the workers they have heading into the holidays, and the hiring they are announcing is largely short-term, seasonal work," said Andy Challenger, chief revenue officer at Challenger, Gray & Christmas. "Companies want the flexibility to meet holiday demand without adding permanent headcount."The reluctance to increase permanent hiring means some unemployed people are experiencing long periods of joblessness.The claims report showed the number of people receiving unemployment benefits after an initial week of aid, a proxy for hiring, increased 23,000 to a still-low seasonally adjusted 1.718 million during the week ended October 24. The so-called continuing claims, however, do not include some unemployed people, including recent college graduates and others who have little or no work history.Some people might also have exhausted their eligibility for benefits, limited to 26 weeks in most states, keeping continuing claims at relatively low levels.The claims report has no bearing on the government's closely watched employment report for October due on Friday as it falls outside the survey period. Nonfarm payrolls likely increased by 65,000 jobs last month after rising 29,000 in September, a Reuters survey of economists showed. The unemployment rate is forecast unchanged at 4.2

Homebuyers today are increasingly seeking greater flexibility and personalization in their residential requirements. Plotted developments offer a compelling proposition through land ownership, customization, and long-term appreciation potential,” said Vimalendra Singh, Chief Business Officer - Residential, Mahindra Lifespace Developers.The proposed development will be the company’s first plotted project outside Mahindra World City in Chennai. In Chennai, Mahindra Lifespace Developers has established a presence in the segment through two projects.The Mumbai-region project marks the company’s entry into a segment that has attracted interest from homebuyers seeking land ownership and the option of building independent homes.Plotted developments have emerged as an alternative to conventional residential projects, with homebuyers showing interest in owning land and having the flexibility to construct homes according to their requirements.Developers are also looking at plotted projects as a way to enter markets where large land parcels are available, without undertaking construction of apartment buildings. The format allows developers to sell individual plots in phases, while buyers can decide the timing and design of construction, subject to applicable regulations.Several developers have been exploring plotted development opportunities as part of their residential portfolios, particularly in locations on the outskirts of major cities, attracting institutional capital and investments from real estate funds into land acquisition and development projects.

articles.title: LIC Q2 Results: Profit jumps 20% YoY to Rs 12,115 crore, NPI grows 16%
articles.summary: Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC), the country's largest insurer, reported a nearly 20% rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 12,114.78 crore for the September quarter on Thursday, supported by strong growth in premium income and higher investment earnings. The state-owned insurer had reported a net profit of Rs 10,098 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. However, profit declined 11% sequentially from Rs 13,584 crore in the June quarter.Net premium income increased 16.2% year-on-year to Rs 1.47 lakh crore from Rs 1.26 lakh crore in the September quarter of FY26. It rose 15% sequentially from Rs 1.27 lakh crore.The growth in premium income was largely driven by a sharp increase in single-premium collections, reflecting higher contributions from policies where customers pay the entire premium upfront.Single-premium income surged 34% to Rs 68,425 crore from Rs 50,882 crore a year earlier. Renewal premium income increased 5% to Rs 68,718 crore from Rs 65,320 crore in the same quarter last year. However, first-year premium income declined 4% to Rs 10,484 crore from Rs 10,884 crore.LIC also reported an increase in investment income during the quarter, providing additional support to profitability.Net investment income in the shareholders' account increased to Rs 2,855 crore from Rs 2,066 crore a year earlier, representing a rise of about 38%.Total income in the shareholders' account increased 11% to Rs 10,527 crore from Rs 9,454 crore. Meanwhile, the insurer's income from investments in the policyholders' account stood at Rs 1.15 lakh crore, compared with Rs 1.12 lakh crore in the year-ago quarter, an increase of around 2.2%.The company reported a surplus of Rs 10,379 crore in the policyholders' account, compared with Rs 9,503 crore a year earlier. The increase in investment income and policyholder surplus contributed to the company's overall financial performance during the quarter.LIC's benefits paid, including claims and other policyholder payouts, increased to Rs 1.34 lakh crore from Rs 1.06 lakh crore in the corresponding quarter last year.Expenses of management rose to Rs 15,143.38 crore from Rs 13,908 crore, an increase of 9%. Net commission expenses increased to Rs 6,089 crore from Rs 5,807 crore a year earlier.LIC's solvency ratio improved to 2.35 as of September 2026, from 2.13 a year earlier. However, the ratio declined sequentially from 2.42 in the June quarter. The insurer's expense of management ratio improved to 10.26% from 12.05% a year earlier, reflecting better cost efficiency.The 13th-month persistency ratio declined to 67.67% from 68.19% a year earlier, while the 25th-month ratio improved marginally to 63.01% from 62.63%.The insurer's investment yield, excluding unrealised gains, declined to 9.04% in the September quarter from 9.33% a year earlier. However, including unrealised gains, the yield increased to 4.10% from 2.07%.

Mistry challenges removal as SDTT trustee
articles.summary: New Delhi: Mehli Mistry has challenged his removal as a trustee of Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and Bai Hirabai Jamsetji Tata Navsari Charitable Institution before the Maharashtra Charity Commissioner, alleging procedural irregularities and violations of trust governance rules.In three rejoinders and applications filed before the Deputy Charity Commissioner, Mistry has questioned the legality of the decisions leading to his removal, the eligibility of certain trustees and their participation in decisions concerning his reappointment.He has also sought an independent inquiry into SDTT's administration, alleging conflicts of interest, improper retention of financial benefits by trustees and irregularities in decisions involving Tata Group companies and the trust's investments in Tata Sons.A key issue raised by Mistry concerns Venu Srinivasan's participation in the decision on his reappointment. Mistry has argued that Srinivasan's tenure as a trustee ended on October 23, 2025, while he communicated his vote against Mistry's reappointment on October 28.Read more: Tata Sons Chairman Chandrasekaran meets Italian PM Meloni after Iveco acquisitionAccording to Mistry, the trust's own records acknowledged that Srinivasan was no longer a trustee when he cast his vote. He has pointed out that a footnote in the records stated that Srinivasan's vote should be disregarded for this reason.However, Mistry contends that removing the vote from the final count does not address the larger issue, as Srinivasan was still included in the decision-making process. He has argued that the entire resolution was invalid because the body considering his reappointment was not properly constituted.Mistry has also disputed the trust's position that his three-year tenure ended on October 28, 2025, requiring a fresh resolution for reappointment. He has cited the SDTT Trust Deed of March 11, 1932, arguing that it does not prescribe a fixed tenure for trustees.He has further relied on an October 17, 2024, joint resolution of SDTT and Sir Ratan Tata Trust, which provided for the reappointment of trustees after the expiry of their tenure without any limitation on the renewed term, subject to applicable law.Read more: Finance Minister Sitharaman urges Tata to resolve feud amicably, rules out govt interventionIn a separate challenge concerning the Bai Hirabai Jamsetji Tata Navsari Charitable Institution, Mistry has questioned the eligibility of trustees under the trust deed. He has cited provisions requiring trustees to profess the Parsi Zoroastrian faith and meet specified residency conditions.On this basis, he has questioned the eligibility of Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh. He has also raised questions about Noel Tata's alleged Irish citizenship and UAE residency, arguing that eligibility requirements should be applied uniformly to all trustees.Mistry has sought affidavits from trustees confirming that they meet the qualifications prescribed under the trust deed. He has also disputed the trust's position that the relevant eligibility provisions are invalid or unenforceable.Separately, Mistry has sought an inquiry into the financial affairs of SDTT, particularly commissions and other benefits allegedly received by trustees serving as nominee directors in Tata Group companies.His application refers to an annual commission of approximately Rs 1.42 crore received by Noel Tata from Tata Sons Private Limited during FY 2024-25, as reflected in corporate filings.He has also raised questions concerning the engagement of Gerry McGovern for Norton Motorcycles, equity infusion into Tata International Limited and alleged deviations from unanimous resolutions on voting the trust's shareholding in Tata Sons.Mistry has argued that such matters could involve conflicts of interest and breaches of fiduciary duties. He has urged the Charity Commissioner to examine corporate filings, declarations of interest, board records and relevant approvals.He has sought rejection of SDTT's preliminary objections and an inquiry or inspection under the Maharashtra Public Trusts Act, 1950.Importantly, Mistry has clarified that he is not seeking reinstatement as an SDTT trustee. Instead, he has sought an examination of the trust's administration and the appointment of an independent administrator, if required, to ensure its proper functioning.Mistry's trusteeship of SDTT and Sir Ratan Tata Trust ended in October 2025 after three trustees opposed his reappointment. On November 4, 2025, he had written to Tata Trusts trustees, including chairman Noel Tata, describing his departure as a harmonious exit and saying he did not wish to drag the charitable institutions into controversy.In the letter, he stressed the need to protect the reputation of the institutions and uphold transparency, good governance and public interest. He also cited a quote attributed to the late Ratan Tata: "Nobody is bigger than the institution it serves."Mistry had earlier filed a caveat before the Maharashtra Charity Commissioner, seeking an opportunity to be heard before any changes were made to the register of trustees.

articles.title: Bharti Airtel Q2 Results: Net profit jumps 31% YoY to Rs 8,887 crore; revenue up 17%; ARPU rises to Rs 271
articles.summary: Bharti Airtel reported a 31% year-on-year (YoY) increase in net profit to Rs 8,887.5 crore for the September quarter (Q2FY27), compared with Rs 6,791.6 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal.The telecom major's consolidated revenue for the quarter rose 16.7% YoY to Rs 60,878 crore, up from Rs 52,145 crore reported in Q2FY26.India mobile revenue grew 10.1% YoY, while ARPU increased to Rs 271 in Q2FY27 from Rs 256 in the year-ago quarter, reflecting improved customer realisations.Operating performance remained strong, with earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) growing 17.8% YoY to Rs 35,240 crore in Q2FY27, compared with Rs 29,919 crore in the year-ago period.India revenue increased 9.4% YoY to Rs 42,308 crore, with the company's mobile business continuing to benefit from premiumisation of its customer portfolio, higher average revenue per user (ARPU) and strong additions in smartphone data customers.The company's Homes business remained another key growth driver, with revenue increasing 25.3% YoY. The segment added 676,000 customers during the quarter, taking its total customer base to 15.4 million.Airtel Business reported an 11.4% YoY increase in revenue, driven by broad-based growth across its core connectivity business and digital services portfolio. Digital TV revenue rose 2.4% YoY to Rs 771 crore, supported by growing adoption of IPTV services.Africa continued to deliver strong growth, with revenue increasing 25.7% YoY in reported currency and 20.6% in constant currency. The business had a customer base of 193.9 million.Airtel's balance sheet also strengthened during the quarter. Its consolidated net debt-to-EBITDA ratio, on an annualised basis, improved to 1.18 from 1.63 as of September 30, 2025. The net debt-to-EBITDAaL ratio, excluding lease obligations, stood at 0.70.The company reported consolidated capital expenditure of Rs 12,467 crore during the quarter, including Rs 9,908 crore in India. It also invested Rs 2,826 crore in a strategic land parcel for its data centre expansion plans in the country.Postpaid additions hit record; smartphone data base expandsOn the operational front, Airtel added 2.9 million smartphone data customers sequentially, taking the number of such users to 81% of its overall mobile customer base. Smartphone data customer additions stood at 18.8 million over the past year.The postpaid segment recorded net additions of 1.2 million customers during the quarter, its strongest-ever performance in a single quarter, taking the overall postpaid base to 31.2 million.Mobile data consumption increased 36.5% YoY to 36.5 GB per customer per month.The company added 497 towers and 11,684 mobile broadband base stations during the quarter. Its network expansion over the past year included 5,649 additional towers and 44,718 kilometres of fibre.Across its operations in 15 countries, Airtel's total customer base expanded to 693 million, supported by quarterly net additions of 12 million customers across India and Africa.Management commentaryCommenting on the performance, Gopal Vittal, Executive Vice Chairman of Bharti Airtel, said the company delivered another quarter of consistent growth, supported by its diversified business portfolio.He highlighted Africa's strong performance, with revenue growing 6.7% sequentially in constant currency, attributing the improvement partly to the deployment of Airtel's homegrown technology stack across markets. India business revenue also recorded healthy sequential growth of 2.7%.Vittal said the India mobile business continued to benefit from the company's portfolio premiumisation strategy and focus on acquiring quality customers. The segment recorded 3.4% sequential revenue growth, while postpaid additions touched a record 1.2 million during the quarter.He also pointed to sustained momentum in the Homes business, which added 676,000 customers, and Airtel Business, which reported 3.8% sequential revenue growth.The company's newer growth initiatives, including financial services and data centres, are also gaining traction, Vittal said. Airtel's investment in a strategic land parcel during the quarter is part of its ambition to build 1 GW of data centre capacity.He added that the company remained focused on maintaining a strong balance sheet, supported by robust cash generation and disciplined capital allocation.Bharti Airtel shares end lowerShares of Bharti Airtel ended Thursday's trading session 0.52% lower at Rs 2,056.90, compared with the previous close of Rs 2,067.60 on the NSE.During the session, the stock traded in a range of Rs 2,048-2,084.The telecom major's shares have declined nearly 3% so far this year. At the prevailing market price, Bharti Airtel had a market capitalisation of approximately Rs 12.84 lakh crore.

AI, data, cyber lead tech hiring at 30.3%
articles.summary: AI, data and cybersecurity represented 30.3% of tech hiring demand in the July–September quarter, up from 25.8% in the preceding quarter, according to a report by staffing and workforce solutions company Quess Corp.India’s global capability centres (GCCs) are directing a greater share of their technology recruitment towards specialists who can deploy AI, manage data and secure enterprise systems, the India GCC Tech Talent Landscape Q2 FY27 report said.Demand for AI, data and analytics professionals grew approximately 14% quarter-on-quarter, while that for cybersecurity and risk management roles increased approximately 12%. Both categories expanded even as overall GCC tech hiring demand declined 3.5%, reflecting continued investment in specialist capabilities within more selective workforce plans.The moderation in demand is consistent with the cyclical hiring patterns of global enterprises, where recruitment typically peaks at the beginning of the calendar year and slows towards year-end.“India’s GCC ecosystem continues to expand, but its growth is also changing the skills companies need,” said Kapil Joshi, CEO – IT staffing at Quess Corp.“As centres expand their responsibilities and explore new talent markets, companies will need to combine specialist hiring with reskilling and internal mobility. This will help them build the capabilities needed to support their growing role in global operations,” Joshi said.Technology and product GCCs recorded the highest share of postings requiring AI and GenAI skills at approximately 32%. Pharma and healthcare saw a five percentage-point increase to approximately 23%, while professional services and consulting rose four percentage points to approximately 22%. Telecom and networks, manufacturing and industrial, and BFSI recorded quarter-on-quarter declines in overall tech hiring demand of approximately 24%, 9% and 8%, respectively.The proportion of postings seeking AI and GenAI skills increased in each industry segment, showing that high-skill roles are gaining importance.Demand within advanced skill clusters also points towards the practical deployment of AI. Applied data science and model operations grew approximately 19%, while cloud security and AI-infused architecture increased approximately 21%. These roles support the deployment, monitoring and management of AI models, alongside secure cloud and enterprise infrastructure.The report estimates a 38–42% supply gap in AI, data and analytics and a 30–35% gap in cybersecurity and risk management.It identified pathways to address these shortages through transitions from adjacent roles, including data scientists moving into model operations, data engineers into applied AI, and cybersecurity analysts into cloud security. Structured reskilling and internal career pathways can complement external recruitment as AI requirements deepen across sectors.Tier-1 cities nevertheless account for approximately 87–88% of advanced-skill hiring and 84–86% of total GCC hiring demand in the country, the report said. But smaller cities are growing faster.Coimbatore stood out with approximately 30% quarter-on-quarter growth in GCC tech hiring demand, helping drive overall tier-2 growth of approximately 13%, compared with 8–10% in Q1 FY27.Among tier-1 cities, Pune was the only market to grow, recording a modest 2% increase, while all other metros saw demand decline. Hyderabad and Mumbai recorded the steepest declines among metros, at approximately 10% and 9%, respectively.India’s GCC workforce is projected to reach 2.7–2.8 million by 2030.

Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Thursday ordered an inquiry into the collapse of a three-storey building under construction in Old Delhi's Chawri Bazar, which claimed two lives and left four others injured, and directed the registration of an FIR against the contractor.
The chief minister also ordered the immediate suspension of the concerned junior engineer (JE) and assistant engineer (AE) in connection with the incident.
She directed officials to ensure the best possible medical treatment for the injured and provide immediate ex-gratia assistance to the affected families.
"Stringent action will be taken against those found responsible, in accordance with the law," the chief minister said.
The building collapsed around 9.50 am in Gali Sitara, near the Chawri Bazar Metro station, police said.

articles.title: India opens deepwater oil, gas bids, offers to fund up to 50% of well costs
articles.summary:
The government is rolling out a special licensing round for deepwater and ultra-deepwater oil and gas blocks, offering monthly bidding windows and relaxed fiscal terms as it prepares to shoulder up to 50 per cent of eligible exploratory well costs under its Rs 84,084-crore Samudra Manthan offshore exploration programme.
The special round under the Open Acreage Licensing Policy (OALP) is aimed at accelerating exploration in India's offshore frontier basins by lowering entry barriers, sharing the high costs and risks of deepwater drilling, and making acreage available to investors throughout the year.
"Under the government's 'Samudra Manthan' National Offshore Exploration Scheme, a Special OALP is being introduced for fast-track award of deepwater and ultra-deepwater (DW/UDW) exploration blocks," the Directorate General of Hydrocarbons (DGH) said in a notice.
DGH said details of the bid round will be announced shortly.
